notes:
Summary: EchoLattice builds a cross-lingual enterprise search layer for regulated verticals (legal, financial). Primary need: high recall across 15–20 languages with per-language precision tuning and predictable cost. They want a hybrid pipeline: ANN retrieval (dense embeddings) for recall, then a lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top-10 to improve precision in languages with scarce training data.

POC goals (customer):
- Validate embeddings quality per language (FR, DE, ES, PT, JA, ZH, AR, RU prioritized) — target recall >= 0.85 on curated eval sets, precision >= 0.75 after rerank.
- Indexing scale target: initial 10M documents, roadmap to 50M within 12 months. Concerned about shard/cluster sizing and index rebuild times.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 250ms for retrieval+rerank (EU region). If reranker pushes above SLO, they prefer fallback to a cheaper re-ranker or reduce k.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming for <$0.03 per query average across mixed workloads (50% retrieval-only, 50% retrieval+rerank). Budget will influence choice between hosted vs Dedicated.
- Model preferences: open multilingual encoders with quantized runtime; interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + quant profiles).

Notes from calls: "We need consistent per-language recall — FR and DE drive enterprise value here, small drop there = lost deals" — CTO Mark Rouss.
"If we can't get enforceable data residency for DE customers we won't move POC forward" — Head of Compliance.

Technical detail snippets:
- Proposed POC: ingest 1M doc subset (mix of PDFs, HTML pages) -> language detection -> per-language embedding pipeline -> ANN index (HNSW/IVF candidate) -> top-100 retrieval -> cross-encoder rerank top-10.
- Perf knobs customer wants to test: continuous batching window, kv-cache sizing for rerank model, quantization (int8/4bit), dynamic k per-language.

Artifacts: demo deck (drive), security FAQ (drive), Fireflies recording of tech call (ff_a8c3d21f), Gmail thread for contract redlines (thread-7b2f9c0e).

POC success criteria (customer):
- Per-language recall >= 0.85 on labeled eval sets for FR/DE/ES
- 95p latency <= 250ms for mixed queries in EU test cluster
- Cost <= $0.03/query for production mix

Next steps (short):
- AE to send POC wiring doc and ingest checklist (Marisol)
- SE to finalize model/quantization test matrix and perf script (Ravi)
- Legal to confirm DE data residency workaround (addendum)

Potential objections: unclear SLA on reranker timeouts; preference for vendor that provides per-language tuning UI (EchoLattice likes Redwood Console features).
use_case_summary: Enterprise RAG stack for multilingual search: dense embeddings for recall + cross-encoder reranking for per-language precision tuning. Focus on indexing scale (10M->50M docs), predictable latency in EU region, and cost-per-query optimizations using quantization and batching.
security_summary: Customer requires SSO/SAML, audit logs integration, KMS-managed keys, and explicit data residency for DE and FR. SOC2 listed as desirable but not blocking; compliance team flagged residency as blocking for select customers.
pricing_notes: Pricing sensitivity: prefers committed capacity if Dedicated reduces per-query cost below $0.03. Wants clear breakdown: retrieval cost vs rerank cost and tradeoffs for top-k. Finance will require a 3rd-month TCO model before procurement.
competitive_landscape_notes: Evaluating Pinecone + Elastic combo and Weaviate. Differentiator for Redwood is unified runtime and Optimize suggestions; customer called out desire for per-language regression alerts and evals tied to prompt sets.
final_commentary: High potential: enterprise pipeline with clear POC metrics. Main risks: residency/legal and meeting 95p latency with cross-encoder in EU. Short timeline to decision if POC shows expected recall + cost numbers.
